description: Zeck free-tier-first provider topology ledger (DEP-001; refreshed by PPR-002 — Live Free-Tier-First Public Preview Deployment). Records, for every provider in providers.json, the tier the public deployment bootstrap selects under the roadmap doctrine order (provider free tier -> usage-based/no-minimum -> low fixed-cost managed -> paid only where required), the CURRENT limits/terms as operational constraints, the degradation path on exhaustion/outage, and the explicit upgrade/exit note. Limits are external facts recorded with an asOf date and a verification status; they are NEVER architecture. PPR-002 refresh (asOf 2026-09-20): every entry now carries its own asOf, source (the provider's public documentation URL, or the repository contract path for repository-defined entries) and verification status; the Cloudflare Queues/Workflows entries moved to doctrine position 1 — both are included on the Workers Free plan with documented free allowances (the preview plane rides the free allowances, usage-based beyond); the Neon, Upstash and Vercel free-tier facts were re-recorded to the 2026-09-20 public baseline. Live verification of provider consoles was NOT RUN in the PPR-002 worker pod (no credentials) — every entry carries verification 'recorded-not-live-verified' and must be re-verified by the credentialed operator at dispatch time (PPR-002 required fact reconciliation; deploy/preflight.ts surfaces this boundary).

verification.detail: Limits below were recorded from the providers' public documentation at the PPR-002 refresh (asOf 2026-09-20; per-entry sources recorded on each tier). NOT RUN: no provider console, quota API or live deployment was queried from the PPR-002 worker pod — no cloud credentials exist there. The credentialed operator (Lead re-run) must re-verify each limit against the provider's current pricing/limits page before provisioning and upgrade the per-entry verification status to live-verified; drift is an operational update to this ledger, never a silent assumption.

selectedTier.selectionRationale: Doctrine position 1 (provider free tier): the authoritative relational concern runs on Neon Free for preview/sandbox exploration; PostgreSQL remains the only durable authority.

tiers.limitsSource: Neon public pricing documentation at https://neon.tech/pricing (recorded at asOf 2026-09-20, PPR-002 refresh; not live-verified in this pod)
tiers.terms: Free tier is for development/evaluation use; production commercial use should move to a paid plan (e.g. Neon Launch) per provider terms.
tiers.upgradeExit: The authoritative concern MUST NOT remain on the free tier for commercial production: promote to Neon Launch (or any managed PostgreSQL provider — the adapter is provider-neutral over the PostgreSQL wire protocol; connection URLs only). Exit path: pg_dump/logical backup through deploy:backup, restore into the replacement through deploy:restore — both are repository-resident drills. The database-port contract (src/platform/db/port.ts) is unchanged by the move. The 100-project / 10-branch-per-project envelope comfortably holds the per-branch preview topology (one project per environment class, one branch per preview).

exhaustionBehavior.effect: Storage/compute exhaustion on the authoritative store fails closed: control-plane admission and every authority-bearing operation refuse. No datastore is silently promoted; no silent paid overage is enabled by default (Neon Free overage is disabled by design; the quota fence denies at the declared limit).

selectedTier.selectionRationale: Doctrine position 1 (provider free tier): artifact bytes (non-authoritative; metadata stays in PostgreSQL) fit the R2 free allowances for preview/sandbox volumes.

tiers.limitsSource: Cloudflare R2 public pricing documentation at https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/pricing/ (recorded at asOf 2026-09-20, PPR-002 refresh; not live-verified in this pod)
tiers.terms: R2 free allowances apply on any plan; usage beyond allowances bills usage-based (no fixed minimum).
tiers.upgradeExit: Non-authoritative bytes: exit to any S3-compatible object store through the D-07 artifact-exit drill (deploy:drill artifact-exit — digest-verified byte migration over two ObjectStorePort endpoints; endpoint+credentials only). The free allowance is disposable headroom, never an operational dependency: artifact metadata/provenance stay authoritative in PostgreSQL.

exhaustionBehavior.effect: Operations requiring artifact bytes fail explicitly; metadata and provenance remain authoritative in PostgreSQL. No artifact bytes fall back through PostgreSQL. Paid overage beyond the free allowance requires the explicit recorded opt-in (quota fence); the default is deny-at-limit.

selectedTier.selectionRationale: Doctrine position 1 (provider free tier, PPR-002 refresh): Queues is included on the Workers Free plan with a documented free allowance (10,000 operations/day, 24-hour free retention), so the preview dispatch transport rides the free allowance first; usage beyond the allowance bills usage-based with no fixed minimum (the doctrine position 2 fallback stays the same provider, no exit needed). The dispatch transport is non-authoritative and backlogs safely in PostgreSQL either way.

limits.value: the queue consumer runs on Workers Free: 100,000 requests/day and 10 ms CPU per invocation

tiers.limitsSource: Cloudflare Queues public pricing documentation at https://developers.cloudflare.com/queues/platform/pricing/ and Workers Free at https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/pricing/ (recorded at asOf 2026-09-20, PPR-002 refresh; not live-verified in this pod)
tiers.terms: Included on the Workers Free plan with the documented free allowance; usage beyond the free allowance bills usage-based per million operations (no fixed minimum) on the owning Cloudflare account. The 24-hour free retention bound is the reason dispatch envelopes carry reference-only correlation pointers and the PostgreSQL authority is the recovery point.
tiers.upgradeExit: Non-authoritative transport: exit to any managed queue/broker implementing the QueueTransportPort contract through the queue-recovery drill (transport substitution + replay convergence through existing dispatch/execution idempotency). Backlogged dispatch is recoverable by design (deploy:queue republish/replay). Staying on Cloudflare beyond the free allowance is usage-based with no fixed minimum — no exit is forced by exhaustion, only by spend policy.

exhaustionBehavior.effect: Execution admission continues through PostgreSQL authority; dispatch defers and backlogs. A queued message is never mistaken for execution success. Spend guardrail: publish attempts are bounded (ZECK_QUEUE_MAX_PUBLISH_ATTEMPTS); the quota fence denies further publishes at the declared spend limit rather than silently continuing paid operations.

selectedTier.selectionRationale: Doctrine position 1 (provider free tier, PPR-002 refresh): Workflows is included on the Workers Free plan with documented free allowances (100,000 requests/day, 3,000 steps/day, 1 GB-month storage), so the preview orchestration rides the free allowance first; usage beyond the allowances bills usage-based with no fixed minimum (the doctrine position 2 fallback stays the same provider, no exit needed). Orchestration is non-authoritative and pauses safely either way.

limits.value: 30 days (documented provider retention; orphaned instances are bounded waste)

tiers.limitsSource: Cloudflare Workflows public pricing documentation at https://developers.cloudflare.com/workflows/platform/pricing/ (recorded at asOf 2026-09-20, PPR-002 refresh; not live-verified in this pod)
tiers.terms: Included on the Workers Free plan with the documented free allowances; usage beyond the allowances bills usage-based on the owning Cloudflare account. Requires a deployed Worker script (Workers Scripts Write token).
tiers.upgradeExit: Non-authoritative orchestration: exit to any durable workflow engine implementing the workflow port contract. Waiting executions live in PostgreSQL (workflow_orchestration.waits is the authority); instances are terminated by compaction and the replacement engine is re-armed by the recovery scan. Staying on Cloudflare beyond the free allowances is usage-based with no fixed minimum — no exit is forced by exhaustion, only by spend policy.

exhaustionBehavior.effect: Waiting orchestrations pause; execution status, budget, policy and ledger state remain authoritative in PostgreSQL and resume on recovery. Instance starts are bounded (ZECK_WORKFLOW_MAX_START_ATTEMPTS); the quota fence denies at the declared spend limit.

selectedTier.selectionRationale: Doctrine position 1 (provider free tier): coordination data is recomputable/bounded/expiring — the textbook free-tier-safe workload.

tiers.limitsSource: Upstash public pricing documentation at https://upstash.com/pricing/redis (recorded at asOf 2026-09-20, PPR-002 refresh; not live-verified in this pod)
tiers.terms: Free tier for evaluation/development; pay-as-you-go beyond.
tiers.upgradeExit: Disposable by doctrine: Redis holds NO authority data (locks, rate limits, dedup hints, cache only). Exit is dropping it — the coordination-degraded mode is a first-class operating state (local runs without Redis by default). Replacement: any managed Redis-compatible service (or local Redis) behind src/platform/redis/port.ts.

exhaustionBehavior.effect: Command-quota or bandwidth exhaustion or outage degrades to conservative local behavior; durable authority is untouched. The monthly command quota makes exhaustion a routine expected state, not an incident.

selectedTier.selectionRationale: Doctrine position 1 (provider free tier) FOR PREVIEW/PERSONAL-NON-COMMERCIAL ONLY: the terms restriction is the binding constraint (ACR-002: Hobby is a development/non-commercial facility; free-tier claims are never commercial entitlements).

limits.value: PROHIBITED — personal/non-commercial development and preview only

tiers.limitsSource: Vercel public pricing documentation at https://vercel.com/pricing (recorded at asOf 2026-09-20, PPR-002 refresh; not live-verified in this pod)
tiers.terms: Vercel Hobby is $0 and restricted to permitted personal/non-commercial use (repository contract, ACR-002, providers.json commercialUse). Commercial production MUST use a commercially permitted plan (Vercel Pro) or an alternate host — the non-commercial preview rail is the boundary.
tiers.upgradeExit: Delivery-only concern: the API is independently runnable (deploy/api.ts; D1.0 section 12) — repoint delivery at any host running the same repository entry with configuration only. Upgrade: Vercel Pro for commercial production; exit: any alternate web/API host (the redundancy alternate in providers.json). Domain authority is unchanged by the repoint (the domain is operator-owned config, never the provider's).

exhaustionBehavior.effect: Hobby bandwidth/function limits make the experience layer unreachable; control-plane and execution-plane authority are unaffected. The degradation is honest at /health (delivery-degraded) and the operator repoints or upgrades — no silent paid overage (Hobby does not overage bandwidth by default).

selectedTier.selectionRationale: Doctrine position 4 (paid only where required): execution compute is a capability/isolation requirement — container isolation cannot be safely satisfied by a shared free-tier HTTP host. The reference deployment self-hosts the runner (zero marginal provider cost) or binds governed customer runners.

limits.value: self-hosted runner cost only; no per-run provider fee

tiers.limitsSource: Repository-defined protocol (deploy/README.md container-runner REST contract); no external provider quota (the source is the repository contract itself, re-confirmed at asOf 2026-09-20 by the PPR-002 refresh).
tiers.terms: First-party fleet runner or a governed customer runner implementing the documented protocol; Zeck validates configurations before the wire.
tiers.upgradeExit: Non-authoritative executor: any runner daemon implementing the documented REST protocol (provider-neutral, no vendor SDK). Absent runner = container substrate reports unavailable and dispatch fails closed; the process substrate still executes.

exhaustionBehavior.effect: Container sandbox dispatch fails closed (runtime-unavailable); executions stay durably recoverable in PostgreSQL and re-dispatch on recovery. No unisolated or ambient-host execution is ever a fallback.

selectedTier.selectionRationale: Doctrine position 2 (usage-based/no-minimum): OTLP/HTTP-JSON is a transport standard; a self-hosted collector (zero cost) or a usage-based managed sink both satisfy the port.

limits.value: bounded by repository constants (buffer maxima, batch sizes, retry attempts are hard-bounded)
self-hosted collector: zero provider cost; managed sink: usage-based

tiers.limitsSource: Repository-defined observability port (src/platform/observability/port.ts); no external provider quota (the source is the repository contract itself, re-confirmed at asOf 2026-09-20 by the PPR-002 refresh).
tiers.terms: Any OpenTelemetry-compatible collector (self-hosted or managed); the protocol is a standard, not a vendor control plane.
tiers.upgradeExit: Unconfigured endpoint is the declared logs-only degraded mode — observability never blocks the control or execution planes. Substitution is endpoint configuration only.

exhaustionBehavior.effect: Endpoint unreachable or unconfigured: the sink degrades to bounded structured local logs with drop counters; overflow is dropped and counted, never buffered unbounded.
